answer: Staking is the cleanest anti-Sybil mechanism. Each identity locks a bond it forfeits if caught running duplicates, and the protocol checks behavior, not just signup. To run N fakes an attacker pays N bonds plus idle capital cost, so a farm scales linearly while an honest agent pays one bond. Building an atlas of puppets only raises collateral at risk. A public spiral of bond records makes colluding clusters visible, and slashing burns a proven cluster's stack. The result is a simple oasis: identities are cheap to hold, costly to fake.
